review_notes: Reviewed unchanged: the accepted alignment partitions all 26 source and all 30 target IDs exactly once and I found no unit to correct.

s001/s002 read under rule 90: one English word for article-plus-participle gives 'who' to the article and 'comforteth' to the participle, matching the rule's own 'hoi epereazontes' -> 'who revile'. Unhedged, as the corpus has it.
s006 versus s008: hemon is free (its only English is 'our'), so rule 20 proper empties the article rather than rule 76's availability arm.
s009/s010 follow rule 61, whose 'pros to dynasthai' -> 'that ... may be able' is this same lemma; rule 24 makes the bare 'that' one analysis with 'to the end that'.
s012 is an expressed accusative subject, so rule 74's supplied-subject question does not arise; 'we' aligns to hemas directly.

s014 keeps 'them ... that' because a prepositional phrase has no verb to carry the relativizer (rules 22, 31, 32), and 'are in' goes to en under rule 53. This is rule 32's 'hoi met' autou' configuration exactly.
s018/s019: because dia is expressed, 'through' answers to the preposition and rule 21's 'of the' bundling is not in play, so the article takes a bare 'the'.

s022/s023: 'we' is the finite verb's inflection-licensed subject under rule 9 and 'ourselves' is autoi's own word. Giving 'we ourselves' whole to autoi would strip the verb of the subject rule 9 licenses, so this is not treated as a live competing analysis.
s024/s025: the 'of' before 'God' realizes the expressed hypo, not a supplied case preposition, so rule 21's prohibition on a bare 'of' on the article and rule 23 both point the same way.
